title: Booking.com Research Reveals There's No Place Like (Someone Else's) Home for Christmas
summary: New Booking.com research reveals Christmas hosting stresses, festive stay trends and why more people are planning to spend Christmas away from home.
body_markdown:
The pressure to pull off the perfect Christmas can take its toll, with nearly half (45%)* saying they spend more time preparing for the big day than enjoying it, according to new research from Booking.com.


**** And with 56% craving a more relaxed celebration, some are now rethinking how and where they spend the festive season.


That doesn't mean the appeal of a full house of family and friends has faded. Nearly half (45%) agree that the chaos of having everyone under one roof is part of what makes Christmas special. Yet 55% admit bringing everyone together isn't easy, and 43%* say they often feel exhausted by Christmas Day.


## **Top 5 Festive Frustrations**


1. Cooking Christmas dinner (21%)


2. The cost of Christmas (19%)


3. Buying & wrapping presents (19%)


4. Food shopping (18%)


5. Cleaning up after guests leave (17%)


And with the average household spending an estimated 13 hours and £770 preparing for Christmas at home, it's perhaps little surprise that attitudes towards hosting are shifting.


For many, spending Christmas away offers a different way to bring people together, with over one in ten (15%) planning to head away this year, as almost a third (32%) say being away from home would make Christmas more enjoyable and exciting for all. A quarter (25%) agree that a getaway on neutral ground would be the fairest compromise with a partner or family.


Renting a holiday home could also ease some of the practical pressures of Christmas, including having enough beds for everyone (16%) and the chance to split costs (14%). The financial strain of hosting can run deep: over one in ten (12%) say they have considered charging family members who stay at theirs over the December break.


The pull of a Christmas away from the family home is strongest among younger adults. Almost half of 18-to-34-year-olds (45%) say they would rent a whole home to celebrate with family or friends, and 49% say a getaway would mean more quality time with loved ones. For one in ten (10%), it's finding a place that feels more Christmassy than their own home.


**Jo Hemmings, Behavioural & Media Psychologist and Relationship Counsellor, says:** “


*With Booking.com seeing a rise in searches for festive stays, it’s clear families are exploring alternatives to hosting Christmas at home. Christmas can bring emotional pressures, particularly when gathering under the family roof means slipping back into old roles and dynamics. Celebrating on neutral ground can help ease tensions, share responsibilities more equally and allow families to focus on enjoying quality time together.”*


Booking.com search data reflects the shift, with searches for country homes up 22% compared to last December for families and farm stays up 25% among groups.*** While Ambleside in the Lake District has seen searches increase by 37%, with Whitby (+32%), Keswick (+26%), Cheltenham and St Ives (both +20%) all appealing for a winter break. For those looking further afield, searches for Ko Lanta in Thailand have risen by 117% year-on-year.****
